assumptions: The rows are aligned; identity is read column by column.
limits: A gap counts as matching anything, so two rows that differ only where one has gaps are 100% identical.
Of a near-identical pair only the shorter row is charged, so a cluster keeps its longest member.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which rows of this alignment are near-copies of a longer row, at what identity?

description: Find the rows of an alignment that repeat another: each row's redundancy is its highest percent identity to a row at least as long (ungapped residues), and a row at or above the threshold is redundant, so filtering keeps the longest representative of each near-identical group. Jalview's definition: a gap matches anything and the pair is compared over the shorter row. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

rows.description: the ALIGNED rows, each {name, aligned}. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences.

threshold.description: percent identity at or above which a row is redundant. In %.

to.description: last column compared, 1-based inclusive; 0 means the last column. Advanced.

name: alignment_redundancy

kept.description: the names of the rows that survive the filter, in alignment order

redundant.description: the redundant rows, each {name, identity}, most redundant first

rows.description: every row's redundancy, {name, identity}, in alignment order

summary.description: how many rows are redundant at the threshold, and which
